messages:
maria: Quick sync — replay harness loadtest shows a 10-15% regression in p99 for the long-context chat workload after the kernel-selector change. Run details: A100-80GB, NVIDIA driver 535.54.03, CUDA 12.2, container redwood/runtime:2026-03-10-gpu-cudnn. Anyone else seeing this?

aj: saw the note in the perf dashboard earlier. I ran a tiny repro on an A100-40GB dev box and p99 looked fine. Could be driver/CUDA combo or a build flag.

devon: important to confirm whether the regression is across synthetic traffic or replay harness. Synthetic tends to have shorter prefixes and different KV cache hit patterns. Which did you run?

maria: replay harness — we replayed production traces so KV cache hit distribution should match prod. Synthetic runs (the usual battlegroup) didn't show the same magnitude.

shawn: can you paste the exact docker image and launch flags? Kernel selection can behave differently with different `LD_PRELOAD` or `TF32` heuristics enabled.

maria: image: `redwood/runtime:2026-03-10-gpu-cudnn`
launch flags: `--runtime-opts="--kernel-selection=v2 --batching=auto --kv-cache=enabled"`

aj: small checklist: 1) driver mismatch (userland CUDA vs kernel driver) 2) container base image glibc/CUDA ABI changes 3) kernel flags (like `MIG` or cgroups CPU pinning affecting batching scheduler). I can repro-run with driver 535 vs 545 matrix.

devon: also post the profiler flamegraph — if the regression is in kernel-selection itself you'll see more time in our selector code vs per-kernel kernels. If it's KV cache thrash you'll see increased attention compute due to more cache misses.

maria: pasted perf-bot link to the run: https://perf.internal/runs/98321 (replay, long-context). Key diff from baseline: selector takes +6ms per request on average, and p99 token latency up ~12ms.

perf-bot: baseline: run/98102 (kernel-selector:v1, driver 535.54.03) ->  p50 18ms p95 62ms p99 110ms
perf-bot: current: run/98321 (kernel-selector:v2, driver 535.54.03) -> p50 19ms p95 70ms p99 122ms

aj: that selector +6ms could be due to more extensive compatibility checks added in v2. We added a fallback check that probes GEMM configuration at runtime — maybe it's not caching results across requests because KV cache layout changed.

maria: here's a short snippet from the replay harness logs showing selector decisions (trimmed):
```
[selector] request_id=abc123 chosen_kernel=matmul_fused_v2 reason=latency_estimate_prefers_v2
[selector] request_id=abc124 chosen_kernel=matmul_legacy reason=compat_fallback
[selector] cache_key=matmul_v2_128x128 not_found
```

devon: that `not_found` is suspicious. We should ensure the selector memoizes per-model+shape across batch boundaries. Replay harness might expose shape variety that synthetic didn't.

shawn: also confirm `ulimit -n` and cgroup thread limits in the harness VMs — different container images bumped worker threads down which can affect batching throughput.

aj: I'm going to run three matrix jobs: (A) driver 535 + runtime:2026-03-10, (B) driver 545 + same runtime, (C) same drivers but with selector v1 vs v2 toggled and `--selector-cache=true`. Will post diffs.

maria: thanks. One more ask — can we capture KV cache hit rate per-request? The replay harness has that metric but it's coarse. If v2 selector changes early kernel selection we might be invalidating KV buckets more often.

perf-bot: scheduled matrix jobs: run/98400 (A), run/98401 (B), run/98402 (C). Expect ~45m each.

ci-bot: build 2026-03-11-7 succeeded for redwood/runtime:2026-03-10-gpu-cudnn (sha: abcdef123)

aj: quick interim: I re-ran a trimmed replay on an A100-80GB with driver 545 and the `--selector-cache=true` flag. p99 returned to baseline within noise (≈+1-2ms). So cache behavior + driver interaction looks like the main axis.

maria: nice. Can you share the exact kernel-level profiler output? A diff that highlights time spent in selector vs GEMM kernels would be ideal.

aj: attaching snippet (trim):
```
-- profile diff --
selector.cpp::choose_kernel +6.1ms
matmul_fused_v2::launch -3.5ms
matmul_legacy::launch +1.2ms
total per-token +3.8ms
```

devon: that matches hypothesis: selector is heavier but chooses faster matmul occasionally, net +3.8ms. Need to decide if selector overhead is worth the wins. For long-context workloads KV cache hit rate increases matmul size, so choice matters.

shawn: ops note — when we flip selector caching on in prod we should stage on Dedicated nodes first and watch p99 for 48h. Also lock the container image and driver combo in the rollout (driver 545 + redwood/runtime:2026-03-10-gpu-cudnn).

maria: action items: 1) aj to open a PR to enable `--selector-cache=true` by default with a feature flag 2) devon to add a per-request KV hit metric to replay harness output 3) shawn to add a Dedicated canary job in infra. I'll file the perf regression ticket and link runs.

aj: PR draft up: https://git.internal/rw/infra/selector-cache/pull/47 — includes tests for memoization across batch boundaries.

devon: I'll extend the harness today to emit `kv_hit_rate` per-request and add a small eval comparing synthetic vs replay distributions.

maria: thanks team. if CI/ops sees anything odd, ping here. :thumbsup:

shawn: noted — scheduling canary for 4h from now.

ci-bot: canary deploy queued -> canary-2026-03-11-13:00 (env: dedicated-canary, driver 545)

maria: closing loop once canary finishes. Anyone want to split off follow-ups or should we keep it here?

aj: keep here for now. I'll post results when matrix jobs finish.

devon: keeping an eye on kv metrics.

perf-bot: matrix jobs completed: 98400(A): p99 +11ms, 98401(B): p99 +2ms, 98402(C): p99 +1ms (with selector_cache). Summary: driver 545 + selector cache restores parity.

maria: perfect. We'll roll selector_cache and pin driver 545 for this rollout. Thanks everyone.
